title: Double crochet (UK)
subtitle: The short, firm everyday stitch, called single crochet in the United States
excerpt: The UK double crochet is the short, dense stitch that makes sturdy fabric. One pull through the stitch, one pull through both loops, and you have a low, firm post. It is the backbone of amigurumi, bags, and anything that needs to hold its shape.
sourceNotes: Reconstructed in our own words from Thérèse de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886), Chapter 9 (Crochet Work), the passage Dillmont titles the plain stitch (Fig. 405), which is the modern UK double crochet. Public domain via Project Gutenberg. UK and US stitch-name equivalences cross-checked against the Craft Yarn Council standard terms.

glossaryTerms.definition: A short, firm crochet stitch worked with no yarn-over before the hook goes in. One of the two most common basic stitches. The UK name; the same stitch is called single crochet in the United States.

The United States name for the stitch British patterns call double crochet. The action is identical; the names differ, which is a frequent source of confusion when working an American pattern from a British background.
The single live loop on the hook between stitches. Every stitch starts and ends with one working loop.

content.text: Insert the hook into the next stitch or chain.
Wrap the yarn over the hook and draw a loop back through. Two loops sit on the hook.
Wrap the yarn over again and pull through both loops at once. One loop remains, and the double crochet is done.
At the start of a row, one chain stands in as the turning chain, though it does not usually count as a stitch.

Double crochet makes the dense, stable fabric you want for amigurumi toys, baskets, bags, potholders, and any piece that needs to keep its shape and not gape. Worked in a spiral it builds the smooth surface of stuffed shapes. It is also the usual edging stitch, giving a neat firm border around a blanket or a garment opening.

Worked into the back loops only, double crochet makes a ridged, slightly stretchy fabric good for soles and cuffs. Two double crochets joined at the top make a smooth decrease for shaping. The half treble is the next stitch up in height, one small step taller and a little softer. Where double crochet feels stiff, moving up a hook size opens the fabric without changing the stitch.
Difficulty: beginner. Double crochet is one of the first two stitches most people learn.
